title: Text 2
subtitle: 大学“成绩宽恕”制度与分数膨胀

sentences.en: Grade inflation — the gradual increase in average GPAs (grade-point averages) over the past few decades — is often considered a product of a consumer era in higher education, in which students are treated like customers to be pleased.
sentences.zh: 分数通胀——过去几十年间平均绩点（GPA）的逐渐上升——通常被视为高等教育消费者时代的产物，在这个时代，学生被当作需要取悦的顾客来对待。

sentences.en: But another, related force — a policy often buried deep in course catalogs called “grade forgiveness” is helping raise GPAs.
sentences.zh: 但另一股相关的力量——一种深藏于课程目录中、名为"成绩宽恕"的政策——正在推高绩点。

sentences.en: Grade forgiveness allows students to retake a course in which they received a low grade, and the most recent grade or the highest grade is the only one that counts in calculating a student’s overall GPA.
sentences.zh: "成绩宽恕"允许学生重修一门成绩较差的课程，在计算学生的总绩点时，只计入最近一次成绩或最高分。

sentences.en: The use of this little-known practice has accelerated in recent years, as colleges continue to do their utmost to keep students in school (and paying tuition) and improve their graduation rates.
sentences.zh: 近年来，随着大学继续竭尽全力留住学生（并让他们继续缴纳学费）并提高毕业率，这种鲜为人知的做法被运用得越来越频繁。

sentences.en: When this practice first started decades ago, it was usually limited to freshmen, to give them a second chance to take a class in their first year if they struggled in their transition to college-level courses.
sentences.zh: 几十年前这种做法刚开始实行时，通常只限于大一新生，目的是让他们在向大学课程过渡遇到困难时，能在第一年获得重修课程的机会。

sentences.en: But now most colleges, save for many selective campuses, allow all undergraduates, and even graduate students, to get their low grades forgiven.
sentences.zh: 但现在，除了许多择优录取的高校外，大多数大学都允许所有本科生乃至研究生免除自己的低分成绩。

sentences.en: College officials also tend to emphasize that the goal of grade forgiveness is less about the grade itself and more about encouraging students to retake courses critical to their degree program and graduation without incurring a big penalty.
sentences.zh: 大学管理人员还往往强调，成绩宽恕的目标与其说关乎分数本身，不如说是为了鼓励学生重修对其学位课程和毕业至关重要的课程，而无需付出重大代价。

sentences.en: “Ultimately,” said Jack Miner, Ohio State University’s registrar, “we see students achieve more success because they retake a course and do better in subsequent courses or master the content that allows them to graduate on time.”
sentences.zh: 俄亥俄州立大学的教务长杰克·迈纳说："归根结底，我们看到学生之所以取得更大的成功，是因为他们重修了课程，在随后的课程中表现更好，或者掌握了足以让他们按时毕业的内容。"

sentences.en: That said, there is a way in which grade forgiveness satisfies colleges’ own needs as well.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，成绩宽恕在某种程度上也满足了大学自身的需求。

sentences.en: For public institutions, state funds are sometimes tied partly to their success on metrics such as graduation rates and student retention — so better grades can, by boosting figures like those, mean more money.
sentences.zh: 对公立院校来说，州政府拨款有时部分取决于它们在某些指标上的表现，如毕业率和学生保持率——因此，更好的成绩可以通过提升这些数字带来更多的资金。

sentences.en: And anything that raises GPAs will likely make students — who, at the end of the day, are paying the bill — feel they’ve gotten a better value for their tuition dollars, which is another big concern for colleges.
sentences.zh: 而且，任何能提高绩点的做法都可能让学生——归根结底，掏钱的是他们——觉得自己的学费花得物有所值，而这也是大学关心的另一大问题。

sentences.en: Indeed, grade forgiveness is just another way that universities are responding to consumers’ expectations for higher education.
sentences.zh: 事实上，成绩宽恕只是大学回应消费者对高等教育期望的另一种方式。

sentences.en: Since students and parents expect a colleges degree to lead to a job, it is in the best interest of a school to turn out graduates who are as qualified as possible — or at least appear to be.
sentences.zh: 既然学生和家长都期望大学学位能带来一份工作，那么学校最好能培养出尽可能合格的毕业生——至少表面看来如此。

sentences.en: On this, students’ and colleges’ incentives seem to be aligned.
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，学生和大学的动机似乎是一致的。

questions.stem: What is commonly regarded as the cause of grade inflation?
questions.analysis: 细节题。根据题干中的关键词grade inflation 可以定位到首段第一句话，此句话的句子主干：“Grade inflation is often considered a product of a consumer era in higher education.” 题干中的be regarded as对应原文中的is considered，题干中的the cause of(后边接结果)与原文中的a product of (前边接结果)都表示因果关系。选项D中consumer是原文中的复现，其他选项都不具备干扰性，因此答案选择D。

questions.stem: What was the original purpose of grade forgiveness?

options.A: To help freshmen adapt to college learning.
options.C: To prepare graduates for a challenging future.
options.D: To increase universities’ income from tuition.

questions.analysis: 细节题。根据题干中的关键词，我们只能定位到文章的第二段，但是第二段讲的是grade forgiveness具体是什么，并没有提及它的目的，然后接下看第三段的首句，出现了this little-known practice指的就是grade forgiveness。而且题干中的the original purpose对应原文中的在第三段第二句话: “When this practice first started decades ago, it was usually limited to freshmen, to give them a second chance to take a class in their first year if they struggled in their transition to college-level courses.”选项A中的freshmen是原词复现，help是对应原文中的give them a second chance，adapt to对应原文中的struggled in their transition to，college learning对应原文中的college-level courses。因此答案为A。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 5, grade forgiveness enables colleges to ______
questions.analysis: 细节题。根据题干中的关键词paragraph 5、grade forgiveness和colleges可以定位到第五段的第一句，即grade forgiveness能够满足学生的需求，但是对应选项并没有对应的答案，所以接着往下看，提到了国家基金与他们的成功有关，得到更好地分数意为这拿到更多的钱。选项A中的financial support指的就是state funds。因此答案为A。

questions.stem: What does the phrase “to be aligned” (Para. 6) most probably mean?

options.C: To be identical with each other.
options.D: To be contradictory to each other.

questions.analysis: 猜词题。根据题干，可以定位到第六段最后一句话：“On this, students’ and colleges’ incentives seem to be aligned.”所以解题的关键是找到this指代的内容。This指代的是前一句话，即：因为学生和家长都希望通过大学学历来找工作，所以学校的最佳利益是尽可能地把学生培养成有能力胜任的人，或者至少看起来是那样。由此可以的出学生和学校的目标是一致的，选项C中的be identical with表示的是与……相同，因此答案为C。

questions.stem: The author examines the practice of grade forgiveness by ______
questions.analysis: 主旨题。题干的字面意思是作者是通过什么样的方式来检验grade forgiveness的实践操作，但是是考查文章的主旨，属于主旨题。阅读每段的段落大意句，可以得出文章主要讲解的是grade forgiveness的原因。因此答案为B。 .ys { width: 610px; margin: 5px; padding: 5px;
